rv.q: The piece achieves a new freshness in this entertaining musicalization, featuring a tuneful score by two Disney veterans...
"A Bronx Tale" is a wildly uneven show — some parts feel just ridiculous in the broadness of their strokes, others entirely charming.
Mostly the piece is too convinced of its own easy dictums.
But let’s face it, this ill-advised musical version, with an anemic score by Alan Menken and Glenn Slater, isn’t going to send ’em dancing up the aisles.
The cast is fine, but seldom electrifying.
For all the craft and polish applied, this musical winds up right in the middle of the wrong place.

But for all its slickness, “A Bronx Tale” is nothing more than a weightless comic-book adaptation of the movie on which it’s based, stripped of the understated yet ever-present sense of threat that gave the film so much of its dramatic force.
This latest iteration of A Bronx Tale, codirected by De Niro and Broadway vet Jerry Zaks, is a dud: a musically unmemorable mix of sappiness and contrived melodrama.
The characters are simple, the storytelling is derivative of better-known musicals ("West Side Story," "Jersey Boys") and the tone is excessively sentimental and solemn.
But if you can be satisfied with this sort of fantastical cityscape, there are far worse ways to burn off a couple of hours than A Bronx Tale .
Chances are this Bronx Tale won’t move you to tears, but Trujillo ensures that it will at least move you a little.
It just doesn’t seem a necessary one.
Too many of the songs are inconsequential, which serves to dilute those ingratiating, low-brow, mob-infused charms which won audiences over in the first (and second) place.
Once again, Cordero is good and sleazy enough so that we never miss the original too much.
Despite the best efforts of its cast and creative team, this once-exciting story comes across stale and banal.

cn.t: Critics find this crowd-pleasing musical derivative and unnecessary, with too-familiar storytelling that struggles to justify its existence beyond the superior film. Mixed reviews praise its entertainment value but cite hackneyed execution and forgettable songs.

vs.sum: The Longacre Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, even from the balcony, and the sound quality is consistently praised. While the seating is a bit narrow, it provides average comfort for most patrons. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant Beaux Arts interior, and facilities are typical for a Broadway venue, with some lines at intermission but generally manageable.

acc.note: Small restroom-only elevator (may not accommodate all wheelchairs). 3 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra.
